options: A program in execution, with its own state and resources
A source file sitting on disk
questions.explanation: The file is a program. A process is that program plus a program counter, registers, memory, and open resources.
traps: The executable file is not yet a process.

questions.prompt: Which items belong in a process control block?
options: Open files, or a pointer to them
The transistor netlist of the ALU
questions.explanation: The PCB is the OS’s record of one process. Hardware diagrams of the ALU are not part of it.

questions.prompt: Two threads of one process share
options: The address space; each has its own registers and stack
One stack pointer and one program counter
questions.explanation: Sharing the address space is the point of threads. Each thread still needs its own PC, registers, and stack, or it could not be in a different place in the code.
traps: If they shared one PC they could not execute two different instructions.

questions.prompt: A process that asked for disk data and cannot run until it arrives is
questions.explanation: It is not on the CPU, and it is not ready to take the CPU. It sits in the waiting state until the I/O completion moves it back to ready.

questions.prompt: A context switch is costly mainly because
options: The OS saves one set of registers and restores another, and caches may go cold
questions.explanation: Direct cost: memory writes for the saved state. Indirect cost: the next process misses in caches and the TLB that the previous one had warmed.

questions.prompt: The ready queue holds processes that
options: Are waiting for a specific I/O completion
questions.explanation: Ready means “runnable”. Waiting processes are on other queues until their event arrives.
traps: Putting blocked processes on the ready queue.

questions.prompt: A zombie process is one that
options: Has exited, but its parent has not yet collected the exit status
Is running on two CPUs at once by definition
Is stored only in the TLB
questions.explanation: The process is not executing. The OS keeps a small record so the parent can observe how it ended.
traps: A zombie is not still running.

options: One process cannot casually read or write another process’s memory
All processes share one address space on purpose
questions.explanation: Each process gets its own translation from virtual addresses to frames. Crossing that boundary requires a system call or other explicit sharing.

questions.prompt: Give one reason to use a second thread instead of a second process.
questions.answer: Threads of one process already share the address space, so they can exchange data without a heavier copy.
questions.explanation: The cost of that convenience is that a bug in one thread can corrupt the others. A second process would be more isolated and more expensive to share with.
